title: US defaults on debt by 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States federal government fails to make a scheduled payment on any Treasury note, bond, or bill at any point between November 5, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, or Fitch publicly classify any U.S. sovereign debt as being in default during the qualifying period this will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, and Fitch.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders assign a 97.3% probability against a U.S. debt default by the end of 2027 because the statutory limit, raised by $5 trillion in July 2025 to $41.1 trillion, is projected to be reached around May 2027, with extraordinary measures extending payment capacity into 2028. Congress has suspended or increased the ceiling nearly 80 times since 1960, and rating agencies expect similar bipartisan action to avoid market disruption. The dollar’s reserve status, deep Treasury market liquidity, and severe economic costs of default reinforce this consensus. A faster-than-expected deficit surge or prolonged 2027 negotiations could compress timelines, though historical patterns and procedural buffers make default by the deadline unlikely.
